action: General advice: as How-To Geek relays, check recent sign-ins and active sessions on your email account from a trusted device, then change passwords and close sessions if anything looks wrong.
date_note: Date is the publication day of Jeremiah Fowler's ExpressVPN report; the page says only that he 'recently discovered' the database and gives no earlier day.
exec: Researcher Jeremiah Fowler reports an unprotected database with approximately 2 billion credentials; its owner is unknown.
geo_basis: no location stated; the database owner is not identified
plain: A researcher found an open database holding approximately 2 billion credentials, apparently from malware logs. Nobody has been identified as its owner, and access was restricted several days after he reported it.
summary: Researcher Jeremiah Fowler reports finding a publicly exposed database, neither password-protected nor encrypted, containing approximately 2 billion credentials in 8,471 folders. He says an estimated 400,000 documents appeared to come from more advanced malware and that the data contained no information identifying its owner. Public access was restricted several days after he reported it to the hosting provider.
title: Researcher reports exposed database holding approximately 2 billion credentials from malware logs

validation.note: Findings are the researcher's own, published by ExpressVPN; How-To Geek relays the same report, so it is one source of the core facts. The database owner has not been identified on either page.

evidence.quote: It contained approximately 2 billion credentials, including email addresses, login names, passwords, and more.
The database contained 8,471 folders with credentials and account information in plaintext.
An estimated 400,000 documents appeared to come from more advanced malware.

review.note: Compared 2 billion, 8,471 folders, 400,000 documents, unknown owner, access restriction and advice against the ExpressVPN report and How-To Geek
